args.rationale:
Investigation of the demand spike trigger reveals that recent daily sales averaging 130 units/day (excluding 3 stockout-censored days on 2026-09-06, 2026-09-07, and 2026-09-08) are driven by active promotion PROMO-1, which ends on 2026-09-23. Extrapolating the promotional sales rate across the full 28-day horizon (ordering 3550 units) is infeasible due to breaching the maximum days of cover policy (63.0 days vs 12-day limit).

Under baseline forecast (50 units/day, total 1400 units demand), the current usable stock of 1000 units leads to a stockout on 2026-10-07 with 400 total unmet units and 12 days below safety stock.

Simulating an order of 600 units from SUP-A at $14.00 per unit arriving on 2026-09-24 (7-day lead time) fully eliminates unmet demand (0 residual unmet units) and leaves closing inventory at 200 units (4.0 days of cover, within the 12-day policy limit). The order satisfies MOQ (300) and pack size (50), fits within storage capacity (peak occupancy 45.00 m³ vs 200.00 m³ limit), and remains well within available budget ($8,400.00 vs $50,000.00 available). Because the spend ($8,400.00) exceeds the autonomy limit of $2,000.00, buyer approval is required.
important_factors: Recent sales of 130 units/day are driven by active promotion PROMO-1 ending 2026-09-23 and should not be extrapolated across the entire horizon.
Baseline projection without order results in a stockout on 2026-10-07 with 400 total unmet units.
Ordering 600 units from SUP-A closes the 400 unmet unit shortage and leaves 200 units in safety stock.
Order cost of $8,400.00 exceeds buyer autonomy spend limit of $2,000.00, requiring buyer approval.
assumptions: Demand returns to the baseline forecast of 50 units/day after promotion PROMO-1 ends on 2026-09-23.
